selection_status: Sender-unseen but analyst-targeted after inspecting the first relay. Not an untouched held-out query benchmark.
assessment_status: Assistant draft obligations; no automatic semantic gold or independent human validation.

questions.question: Suppose Tuesday passes with no reply. What action is licensed by the writer's plan, and does the alternative Monday arrangement automatically replace waiting? Explain the dependency.
questions.source_anchor: must wait till I do hear
questions.source_obligation: Wait; silence is not confirmation that the alternative suits the hosts. Do not automatically book Monday.

questions.question: Suppose a Tuesday reply says Wednesday is impossible but the following Monday suits the hosts better. Which alternative arrangement becomes applicable, and who is to provide it? Distinguish a conditional arrangement from evidence that the journey happened.
questions.source_anchor: promise to take me to Greenwich
questions.source_obligation: Edward's conditional Monday Greenwich arrangement applies; no completed journey is established.

questions.question: Suppose the reply instead confirms the hosts can receive the writer on Wednesday. Does that remove her stated obstacle to accompanying Frank, and does the document establish that she actually departed? Keep permission and occurrence separate.
questions.source_anchor: I cannot go on the uncertainty
questions.source_obligation: Removes stated lodging uncertainty, not proof of departure.

questions.question: What commitment, if any, has Edward made? Identify how firmly the document presents it and the conditions still attached. Do not upgrade an offer, promise, or possibility into a completed action.
questions.source_anchor: Edward has been so good as to promise
questions.source_obligation: Original states a conditional promise. Relay says offered; distinguish literal wording from contested pragmatic equivalence.

questions.question: Does silence on Tuesday establish Mary's actual location, or only the writer's working assumption? Explain how that epistemic distinction affects the travel decision.
questions.source_anchor: I must suppose Mary is not at home
questions.source_obligation: Assumption of absence, not established location; still waits.

questions.question: Can a travel log mark the invitation to Steventon as accepted and the visit as completed? State which parts of the interaction are established and which remain unknown.
questions.source_anchor: after having invited her to go to Steventon with me
questions.source_obligation: Invitation made; acceptance and completion unknown.

questions.question: Suppose a publisher proposes that the author bear all financial risk but receive half the profits. Is that compatible with the writer's stated boundary? Distinguish a hypothetical acceptable arrangement from an agreement already reached.
questions.source_anchor: I would not publish on my sole risk
questions.source_obligation: Incompatible because sole risk is refused, irrespective of profit share; no agreement reached.

questions.question: A negotiator asks for the exact illustrative fractions of risk and profit mentioned by the writer. What fractions, if any, can be recovered, and are they an example or an exclusive requirement? Do not invent unspecified numbers.
questions.source_anchor: such as half risk and half profit
questions.source_obligation: Half each, as an example, not a mandatory sole acceptable split. Relay supplies no exact fraction.

questions.question: When planning the book's audience, distinguish readability from predicted interest. What explicit restriction, if any, does the document place on who would be interested? Do not infer an exclusion merely from naming a positive audience.
questions.source_anchor: who care for Natural History, but no others
questions.source_obligation: Original explicitly excludes others in the writer's prediction, while also discussing accessibility. Relay only names a positive audience.

questions.question: Who is said to object to, or worry about, very short books, and with what degree of certainty? Separate an opinion attributed to the recipient from the writer's own general doubts and possible overvaluation.
questions.source_anchor: I believe you think very little books objectionable
questions.source_obligation: Writer believes recipient objects; writer also has own doubts. Relay assigns the short-book worry to the writer.

questions.question: Suppose the recipient privately doubts separate publication is worthwhile but recommends it solely to please the writer. Would that fulfil the request? Explain how the promise to follow advice interacts with the demand for candour.
questions.source_anchor: I beg you not to be guided in the least in order to oblige me
questions.source_obligation: No; willingness to follow advice does not waive the request for candid judgment.

questions.question: Can the publication decision already be treated as settled because the writer completed the paper and proposes possible terms? Identify the remaining decision dependency and whether a recipient response is recorded.
questions.source_obligation: Advice requested and separate publication tentative; no recipient acceptance or final agreement recorded.

questions.question: Would the beginning of March by itself establish that the stated financial barrier to travelling south has ended? State the most precise time boundary supplied, without turning it into a confirmed travel date.
questions.source_anchor: until the session is over (end of March)
questions.source_obligation: No; original says session over at end of March, without a definite trip date. Relay retains session ending in March but drops end-of-month precision.

questions.question: Does the document identify what institution or kind of session determines the travel timing? Give only the identification actually present, or state that it is unspecified.
questions.source_obligation: Original does not identify its type. Relay explicitly calls it parliamentary; distinguish faithful reading from source fidelity.

questions.question: Colvin reads the message as saying his company is unwanted. Is that interpretation supported? Reconcile the writer's desire, concern about imposing, and uncertainty about the household's readiness.
questions.source_obligation: Company desired, but writer will not impose; father's fitness remains uncertain.

questions.question: Suppose the writer receives enough money tomorrow. Does that establish that his father is fit to receive Colvin or that a visit is booked? Separate the constraints changed by this supposition from those it does not resolve.
questions.source_anchor: still not quite certain whether my father will be quite fit for you
questions.source_obligation: Money does not settle father's fitness or book a visit. Avoid claiming it removes every constraint.

questions.question: Construct the stated work sequence: the unfinished story, the proposed Portfolio paper, and the offer made to Appleton. Which depends on finishing something else, and which lacks a reply? Do not turn a plan for a paper into an established publication date.
questions.source_anchor: so soon as I am done with this story
questions.source_obligation: Portfolio paper follows story completion; Appleton's separate French-poet proposal has no reply; no publication date.

questions.question: Compare the certainty of the story's depiction of Renaissance Italy with the certainty of the name used for the French poetic school. What does the document mark as imagination or tentative naming, if anything? Do not import external literary knowledge.
questions.source_anchor: the Parnassiens, I think they call them
questions.source_obligation: Original: Italy imagined, school name tentative. Relay: imagined Italy retained, school named without the hesitation.
